recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce accepted into Request.status or ServiceRequest.status unless a later work-group decision changes the Request pattern separation between authorization status and fulfillment status.
issue_request: FHIR-6876 is a Published/Persuasive Patient Care ballot comment asking how ReferralRequest.status code active differed from accepted. The final resolution says ReferralRequest status was aligned with the Request pattern through GF/FHIR-10293 so the status value set has active and not accepted.
initial_application: No commit explicitly names FHIR-6876. The linked application path is FHIR-10293/GF#10293: commit f4d7536caa07670c028ba0bc114a334b142e7b9a changed ReferralRequest.status from the local referral-request-status value set to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/request-status and removed the local ReferralRequest status value-set worksheet. Earlier commit b40ce8e28558ce4b7a692f4fa9b0ea24b8bd5c38 had added accepted for FHIR-3827, which the later workflow alignment superseded.
additional_context: ReferralRequest is not an active current resource; source/fhir.ini lists ServiceRequest in [resources] and records that ReferralRequest became ServiceRequest. Current ServiceRequest.status requires ValueSet/request-status, whose CodeSystem includes active but no accepted code. Request pattern narrative separates requester-controlled request status from fulfillment states such as requested, accepted, and in-progress, which are tracked by Task or event resources. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the build-scope source already omits accepted from ServiceRequest/Request status codes and explains that acceptance belongs to fulfillment tracking rather than request authorization status.

related_jiras.note: Workflow standardization issue named by FHIR-6876's resolution and implemented by the relevant GF#10293 source commits.
Earlier Published issue added accepted to ReferralRequest.status; the later FHIR-6876/FHIR-10293 workflow alignment removed that local status in favor of Request.status.
Duplicate ballot comment with the same active-versus-accepted question.
